question: Should separately published official plugins receive a deliberately supported runtime facade, or should this PR expose the current production-private `plugin-sdk` subpaths as JavaScript-only package exports?
rationale: Both paths can make the immediate package import succeed, but they create materially different external compatibility contracts and repository policy favors owner-defined facades or generic contracts over private internal imports.

options.title: Add a supported runtime facade
options.body: Provide the narrow official-plugin runtime capability through a documented or registry-aware facade and migrate affected plugins away from private subpaths.

options.title: Accept runtime-only exports
options.body: Treat the JavaScript-only exports as an intentional external compatibility surface and document ownership, upgrade expectations, and a removal/deprecation policy.

options.title: Pause for packaging redesign
options.body: Hold this PR while maintainers define the external official-plugin runtime contract before widening package exports.

recommendation.title: Add a supported runtime facade
recommendation.body: Provide the narrow official-plugin runtime capability through a documented or registry-aware facade and migrate affected plugins away from private subpaths.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the member author and assignee with the direct packaging reproduction and implementation context; final contract direction still needs maintainer confirmation.
